gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a battery level that a named reviewer saw on a solar camera in bad weather or with no sun. Examples: WhistleOut's eufy SoloCam S340 never dropped below 91% through days of non-stop rain, Mighty Gadget's Reolink Argus 4 Pro fell to about 25% after about three weeks on battery alone, and Reviewed's Arlo Essential Solar held only 50–75% with 4–5 hours of October sun.
standout_why: Both saved ChatGPT chats ran no search, so they got no results and cited no rival pages. The answer gives only generic advice ('5–10W or more' panel, battery 'sized for several cloudy days') and no measured result for any product. These measured battery levels from named reviewers are therefore all new. They don't settle a single pick on their own, because each reviewer tested in different conditions.
decides: This confirms that how well the solar input keeps up matters more than battery size. The S340, with its panel built into the camera, stayed at 91% or higher through rain in WhistleOut's test. The Reolink Argus 4 Pro (Dealectric lists its 6 W solar kit) read 100% through a sunny week but drained to about 25% in about three weeks with no solar charging, so the shopper should buy the kit with the panel rather than the camera alone. The Arlo Essential Solar's built-in 1.2 W panel gave mixed results: CNET saw 97% with about an hour of sun a day, Reviewed saw 50–75% with 4–5 hours in October. That makes it a weaker pick for shaded or northern spots.
